tenets.label: The right size of a political unit

ideologies.name: Marxism-Leninism
ideologies.blurb: A vanguard party seizes state power and uses it to build socialism through central planning.

ideologies.name: Stalinism
ideologies.blurb: Marxism-Leninism concentrated in a single leader, industrialised at speed and defended by terror.

ideologies.name: Maoism
ideologies.blurb: Revolution carried by the peasantry from the countryside, with continuous struggle against new bureaucratic elites.

ideologies.name: Marxism-Leninism-Maoism
ideologies.blurb: Maoism codified as a universal third stage of revolutionary science rather than a Chinese application.

ideologies.name: Hoxhaism
ideologies.blurb: Every other socialist state betrayed Marxism-Leninism; the correct response is doctrinal purity and national isolation.

ideologies.name: Dengism
ideologies.blurb: Markets and private enterprise are tools a communist party may use to develop the productive forces.

ideologies.name: Xi Jinping Thought
ideologies.blurb: Party discipline, national rejuvenation and state-directed technology, tightening what Dengism loosened.

ideologies.name: Titoism
ideologies.blurb: Enterprises run by their own workers' councils, in a federal socialist state aligned with neither bloc.

ideologies.name: Castroism
ideologies.blurb: Anti-imperialist national liberation fused with a one-party socialist state and universal welfare.

ideologies.name: Guevarism
ideologies.blurb: A small armed vanguard in the countryside can create the conditions for revolution rather than wait for them.

ideologies.name: Sandinismo
ideologies.blurb: National liberation, mixed economy and Christian base communities in one revolutionary front.

ideologies.name: Ho Chi Minh Thought
ideologies.blurb: National independence first, socialism through it, with communist organisation serving the anti-colonial war.

ideologies.name: Juche
ideologies.blurb: A nation must be entirely self-reliant in politics, economy and defence, answerable to nothing outside itself.

ideologies.name: Kimilsungism-Kimjongilism
ideologies.blurb: Juche codified around a hereditary leader and an army-first ordering of society.

ideologies.name: Eurocommunism
ideologies.blurb: Communist parties accepting parliamentary democracy, civil liberties and a road to socialism through the ballot.

ideologies.name: Kádárism
ideologies.blurb: Political obedience traded for consumer comfort and a quiet private life inside a one-party state.

ideologies.name: Ceaușescu's national communism
ideologies.blurb: Stalinist central planning turned nationalist and pronatalist, independent of Moscow and closed to everyone.

ideologies.name: Khrushchevism
ideologies.blurb: Socialism competes with capitalism by out-producing it, not by war, and without the terror.

ideologies.name: Bukharinism
ideologies.blurb: Socialism reached at a peasant's pace, through the market and voluntary cooperation rather than forced collectivisation.

ideologies.name: Browderism
ideologies.blurb: Communists should dissolve into a broad national coalition and pursue socialism as loyal citizens.

ideologies.name: Lovestoneism
ideologies.blurb: American capitalism is strong enough that revolutionary strategy must be built for its conditions, not Russia's.

ideologies.name: Sultan-Galievism
ideologies.blurb: Whole colonised nations, not just workers, are the proletariat — so Muslim national liberation is the revolution.

ideologies.name: Gonzalo Thought
ideologies.blurb: Protracted people's war led by an infallible guiding thought, with terror as a deliberate instrument.

ideologies.name: Prachanda Path
ideologies.blurb: People's war in the countryside followed by entry into parliament, in a federal republic.

ideologies.name: Naxalism
ideologies.blurb: Armed agrarian revolution in India's forest belt, rejecting the parliamentary road entirely.

ideologies.name: Nkrumaism
ideologies.blurb: Africa can only be free if it unites continentally; socialism and pan-African political union are one project.

ideologies.name: Ujamaa
ideologies.blurb: Socialism grown from the traditional extended family and the village, not from industrial class struggle.

ideologies.name: Sankarism
ideologies.blurb: Anti-imperialist self-reliance with women's emancipation and desert reforestation as revolutionary tasks.

ideologies.name: Trotskyism
ideologies.blurb: Revolution must spread internationally at once; the USSR was a workers' state deformed by a bureaucratic caste.

ideologies.name: Pabloism
ideologies.blurb: Revolutionaries should bury themselves inside mass reformist parties for a whole historical period.

ideologies.name: Posadism
ideologies.blurb: Nuclear war would destroy capitalism and clear the way for socialism, and advanced extraterrestrials would be socialists too.

ideologies.name: Third Camp socialism
ideologies.blurb: Both superpowers were class enemies; the Soviet bureaucracy was a new exploiting class, not a degenerated workers' state.

ideologies.name: Bureaucratic collectivism
ideologies.blurb: The Soviet bureaucracy owned the means of production collectively and was therefore a genuine ruling class.

ideologies.name: State capitalism theory
ideologies.blurb: The Eastern bloc was capitalism run by the state, competing militarily on the world market like any firm.

ideologies.name: Council communism
ideologies.blurb: Workers' councils are the form of the revolution; parties and unions can only substitute themselves for the class.

ideologies.name: Bordigism
ideologies.blurb: The party holds the invariant programme regardless of what workers currently believe; democracy is no measure of truth.

ideologies.name: Luxemburgism
ideologies.blurb: The mass strike teaches the class what no party can; revolution without democracy becomes bureaucratic rule.

ideologies.name: Communisation theory
ideologies.blurb: Communism is not a society built after the revolution but the immediate abolition of value, work and class in the act itself.

ideologies.name: Situationism
ideologies.blurb: Capitalism has become a spectacle of images; the task is to destroy separation and construct lived situations.

ideologies.name: Autonomism
ideologies.blurb: Workers' own refusal drives capitalist development; struggle needs no party and increasingly no factory either.

ideologies.name: Johnson-Forest Tendency
ideologies.blurb: Ordinary workers and Black Americans are already theorising their own liberation; the intellectuals should record it.

ideologies.name: Marxist humanism
ideologies.blurb: Marx's core is alienation and human self-realisation, not economic laws or party discipline.

ideologies.name: Bogdanovism
ideologies.blurb: A universal science of organisation, and a proletarian culture built by workers before any seizure of power.

ideologies.name: God-Building
ideologies.blurb: Socialism needs the emotional force of religion, with humanity itself as the deity being constructed.

ideologies.name: De Leonism
ideologies.blurb: Workers organise industrially to take over production, and use the ballot only to dissolve the political state.

ideologies.name: Impossibilism
ideologies.blurb: No reform is worth supporting; socialism arrives only when a majority understands and votes for it, worldwide and at once.

ideologies.name: Sorelianism
ideologies.blurb: The general strike works as a mobilising myth; heroic violence by producers renews a decadent society.

ideologies.name: Left Opposition
ideologies.blurb: Rapid industrialisation and party democracy against the rising bureaucracy, before it consolidated.

ideologies.name: Anarcho-communism
ideologies.blurb: No state, no wages, no money — free federations taking from a common store according to need.

ideologies.name: Anarcho-syndicalism
ideologies.blurb: Revolutionary unions both fight capital now and become the structure that runs production afterwards.

ideologies.name: Collectivist anarchism
ideologies.blurb: Collective ownership of the means of production, but people are still paid for the labour they contribute.

ideologies.name: Platformism
ideologies.blurb: Anarchists need a disciplined organisation with a common line — theoretical unity and collective responsibility.

ideologies.name: Especifismo
ideologies.blurb: A specifically anarchist organisation works inside broader popular movements without trying to lead them.

ideologies.name: Synthesis anarchism
ideologies.blurb: Communists, syndicalists and individualists should share one organisation rather than split over the future.

ideologies.name: Makhnovism
ideologies.blurb: Armed peasant self-defence holding free territory against every state that claimed it.

ideologies.name: Magonism
ideologies.blurb: Land and liberty — indigenous communal landholding as the base of an anarchist revolution.

ideologies.name: Communalism
ideologies.blurb: Face-to-face citizen assemblies in each municipality, confederated upward, with ecology as the organising insight.

ideologies.name: Democratic confederalism
ideologies.blurb: Stateless self-administration through councils, with women's liberation and ecology written into its foundations.

ideologies.name: Zapatismo
ideologies.blurb: Indigenous autonomy governed by assemblies whose delegates lead by obeying, refusing to take state power.

ideologies.name: Anarcho-pacifism
ideologies.blurb: The state rests on violence, so it must be dissolved by refusal and non-cooperation rather than by force.

ideologies.name: Christian anarchism
ideologies.blurb: No one may rule another because only God is sovereign; the Sermon on the Mount forbids the state's violence.

ideologies.name: Anarcho-naturism
ideologies.blurb: Liberation from the state and from civilisation's habits together — nudism, vegetarianism and rural communes as anarchist practice.

ideologies.name: Veganarchism
ideologies.blurb: Human and animal liberation are one struggle against domination; anarchism that eats animals is incomplete.

ideologies.name: Anarcho-transhumanism
ideologies.blurb: Technology should be seized and distributed to abolish every biological and social constraint on freedom.

ideologies.name: Queer anarchism
ideologies.blurb: The state, the family and gender itself are linked systems of domination to be abolished together.

ideologies.name: Anarcha-feminism
ideologies.blurb: Patriarchy is the oldest hierarchy; no revolution that leaves the household untouched is a revolution.

ideologies.name: Mutualism
ideologies.blurb: Property is legitimate only where you occupy and use it; free credit and worker associations replace capitalism without a state.

ideologies.name: Individualist anarchism
ideologies.blurb: The sovereign individual in a free market stripped of the four monopolies the state grants to capital.

ideologies.name: Egoism
ideologies.blurb: Every cause above you — state, God, humanity, morality — is a spook; only your own interest is real.

ideologies.name: Egoist communism
ideologies.blurb: Communism chosen selfishly — the union of egoists finds abundance more satisfying than property.

ideologies.name: Illegalism
ideologies.blurb: Theft and expropriation are not merely tolerable but the honest response of an individual at war with society.

ideologies.name: Insurrectionary anarchism
ideologies.blurb: Permanent attack by small informal groups, refusing to wait for mass organisations that never arrive.

ideologies.name: Agorism
ideologies.blurb: Build the black market until it starves the state — revolution by untaxed trade rather than by ballot or bullet.

ideologies.name: Left-wing market anarchism
ideologies.blurb: Genuinely free markets would dissolve corporations and bosses; capitalism survives only on state privilege.

ideologies.name: Voluntaryism
ideologies.blurb: Every human relationship must rest on consent; no one may be governed, taxed or conscripted without agreeing.

ideologies.name: Panarchism
ideologies.blurb: Choose your government the way you choose a religion — many regimes on the same territory, each with its own subscribers.

ideologies.name: Ontological anarchism
ideologies.blurb: Don't seize the state — open temporary zones of freedom that dissolve before power can find them.

ideologies.name: Mutual banking
ideologies.blurb: The single reform that matters is credit at cost; interest is the tax that makes capitalism possible.

ideologies.name: Anarcho-monarchism
ideologies.blurb: A powerless ceremonial king above, and no state at all below — hierarchy as symbol rather than as administration.

ideologies.name: Bolo'bolo
ideologies.blurb: The planet reorganised into several hundred autonomous communities of about five hundred people, each with its own way of life.

ideologies.name: Neoism
ideologies.blurb: An anti-movement of shared pseudonyms and deliberate contradiction, refusing identity as a political act.

ideologies.name: Anarcho-capitalism
ideologies.blurb: Every service the state provides, courts and police included, should be bought on the market from competing firms.

ideologies.name: Hoppeanism
ideologies.blurb: Anarcho-capitalism with covenant communities that may exclude whomever they like, and a low opinion of democracy.

ideologies.name: Neocameralism
ideologies.blurb: Run the state as a profitable corporation with shareholders and a CEO; residents are customers, not citizens.

ideologies.name: Seasteading
ideologies.blurb: Found new sovereign communities on the ocean so that governance itself faces competition and exit.

ideologies.name: Network state
ideologies.blurb: Build an online community with shared values first, crowdfund territory second, seek recognition last.

ideologies.name: Crypto-anarchism
ideologies.blurb: Strong cryptography makes taxation and censorship technically impossible, so the state simply stops working.

ideologies.name: Charter cities
ideologies.blurb: Import good rules into a poor country by building new cities under a separate legal charter.

ideologies.name: Paleolibertarianism
ideologies.blurb: Free markets joined to cultural traditionalism, hostile to both the welfare state and social liberalism.

ideologies.name: Free State Project
ideologies.blurb: Concentrate enough libertarians in one small jurisdiction to actually take it over and shrink it.

ideologies.name: Classical liberalism
ideologies.blurb: Limited constitutional government, free trade and individual rights as the framework for everything else.

ideologies.name: Minarchism
ideologies.blurb: A state limited strictly to courts, police and defence — legitimate, but nothing beyond that.

ideologies.name: Objectivism
ideologies.blurb: Rational self-interest is a virtue and altruism a vice; laissez-faire capitalism follows from that ethics.

ideologies.name: Manchester liberalism
ideologies.blurb: Free trade between nations makes war unprofitable and empire pointless; peace follows commerce.

ideologies.name: Philosophic Radicalism
ideologies.blurb: Every institution judged only by whether it produces the greatest happiness, and reformed if it does not.

ideologies.name: Neoclassical liberalism
ideologies.blurb: Free markets justified precisely because they serve the worst off, with a floor beneath everyone.

ideologies.name: Left-libertarianism
ideologies.blurb: Absolute self-ownership, but natural resources belong to everyone equally — so land rents must be shared out.

ideologies.name: Libertarian paternalism
ideologies.blurb: Leave every option open but arrange the defaults so people tend to choose well.

ideologies.name: Neoliberalism
ideologies.blurb: Markets need an active state to construct and defend them; competition should organise as much of life as possible.

ideologies.name: Ordoliberalism
ideologies.blurb: A strong state must write and enforce the rules of competition, then never intervene in outcomes.

ideologies.name: Social liberalism
ideologies.blurb: Freedom means the actual capacity to act, so the state must provide the conditions for it.

ideologies.name: Rawlsian liberalism
ideologies.blurb: Inequalities are permitted only where they improve the position of the least advantaged.

ideologies.name: Luck egalitarianism
ideologies.blurb: People may keep what follows from their choices but not what follows from their luck.

ideologies.name: Property-owning democracy
ideologies.blurb: Spread capital ownership widely before markets act, rather than taxing and transferring afterwards.

ideologies.name: Civic republicanism
ideologies.blurb: Freedom is not being subject to anyone's arbitrary power, which requires active citizenship and contestable government.

ideologies.name: Radical democracy
ideologies.blurb: Conflict is permanent and healthy; democracy means keeping it open rather than dissolving it into consensus.

ideologies.name: Deliberative democracy
ideologies.blurb: Legitimacy comes from reasoned public argument that anyone affected could in principle accept.

ideologies.name: Social democracy
ideologies.blurb: Capitalism kept but tamed — strong unions, universal welfare and redistribution through parliament.

ideologies.name: Democratic socialism
ideologies.blurb: Socialism, not a softer capitalism — public ownership of the commanding heights, won democratically.

ideologies.name: Fabianism
ideologies.blurb: Socialism arrives by inevitable gradualness, through expert administration and patient permeation of institutions.

ideologies.name: Bernsteinian revisionism
ideologies.blurb: Capitalism is not collapsing, so the movement is everything and the final goal nothing.

ideologies.name: Nordic model
ideologies.blurb: Open competitive markets plus very high taxes, universal services and centrally bargained wages.

ideologies.name: Labourism
ideologies.blurb: The trade unions in parliament, defending members' wages and conditions without a theory of society.

ideologies.name: Austromarxism
ideologies.blurb: Neither reform nor putsch — win a real majority, and solve the national question by personal cultural autonomy.

ideologies.name: Market socialism
ideologies.blurb: Social ownership of capital with prices and competition retained to allocate it.

ideologies.name: Lange model
ideologies.blurb: A central board sets prices by trial and error, reproducing the market's efficiency without private owners.

ideologies.name: Liberal socialism
ideologies.blurb: Socialism as the fulfilment of liberalism's promise, never as a reason to suspend its liberties.

ideologies.name: Ethical socialism
ideologies.blurb: Socialism is a moral claim about fellowship and dignity, not a conclusion drawn from economic laws.

ideologies.name: Guild socialism
ideologies.blurb: Industry run by national guilds of its own workers, with the state representing consumers alongside them.

ideologies.name: Economic democracy
ideologies.blurb: Extend the vote into the firm: workers control the workplace and society controls investment.

ideologies.name: Wage-earner funds
ideologies.blurb: Company profits gradually transferred into union-controlled funds until the workers own the economy outright.

ideologies.name: Chavismo
ideologies.blurb: Oil revenue redistributed through communal councils, with a charismatic leader against the old elite.

ideologies.name: Georgism
ideologies.blurb: Tax the unimproved value of land and nothing else; land rent belongs to everyone, what you build belongs to you.

ideologies.name: Geolibertarianism
ideologies.blurb: Full libertarian self-ownership joined to the claim that no one may privately pocket the rent of the earth.

ideologies.name: Geoanarchism
ideologies.blurb: Land rent collected and shared by voluntary communities with no state to collect it.

ideologies.name: Single-tax movement
ideologies.blurb: One tax on land replaces every other levy — on wages, buildings, trade and industry alike.

ideologies.name: Georgist environmentalism
ideologies.blurb: Extend land rent to every natural resource and sink, so pollution and sprawl carry their true price.

ideologies.name: Physiocracy
ideologies.blurb: Only land produces genuine surplus, so tax it alone and leave commerce entirely free.

ideologies.name: Ricardian socialism
aliases: labour's right to the whole produce
ideologies.blurb: Labour creates all value, so rent and profit are simply deductions from what the worker is owed.

ideologies.name: Commons trusteeship
ideologies.blurb: Natural wealth held in trust for everyone, paying an equal dividend out of what it earns.

ideologies.name: Freiwirtschaft
ideologies.blurb: Money that loses value if hoarded, so it circulates like goods and interest falls to zero.

ideologies.name: Local scrip currency
ideologies.blurb: Towns issue their own circulating money so that local trade never stops for lack of national currency.

ideologies.name: Social Credit
ideologies.blurb: Wages never suffice to buy what industry makes, so the state must issue a dividend to close the gap.

ideologies.name: Alberta Social Credit
ideologies.blurb: Social Credit as a governing prairie party — dividends, monetary heresy and evangelical Protestantism together.

ideologies.name: Binary economics
ideologies.blurb: Capital, not labour, produces most output — so finance must be arranged to make every citizen an owner of it.

ideologies.name: Share Our Wealth
ideologies.blurb: Cap great fortunes outright and hand every family a homestead and a guaranteed income.

ideologies.name: Townsend Plan
ideologies.blurb: A generous pension for everyone over sixty, on condition it is spent within the month.

ideologies.name: Bellamyite Nationalism
ideologies.blurb: The whole economy as one national trust, everyone serving a term in an industrial army for an equal share.

ideologies.name: Modern monetary politics
ideologies.blurb: A currency-issuing state is limited by real resources, not by revenue, so full employment is always affordable.

ideologies.name: Basic income maximalism
ideologies.blurb: One unconditional payment large enough to live on, replacing the conditional welfare apparatus entirely.

ideologies.name: Full-reserve banking
ideologies.blurb: Strip private banks of the power to create money and give it back to a public authority.

ideologies.name: Mutual credit systems
ideologies.blurb: Communities keep their own ledger of favours and goods, with no interest and no national money involved.

ideologies.name: Revolutionary syndicalism
ideologies.blurb: The union is the revolutionary organ and the general strike its weapon; politics is a distraction.

ideologies.name: Mondragonism
ideologies.blurb: A federation of worker cooperatives with its own bank and university, competing in ordinary markets.

ideologies.name: Rochdale cooperativism
ideologies.blurb: Consumers own the shops, one member one vote, with the surplus paid back as a dividend.

ideologies.name: Worker self-directed enterprise
ideologies.blurb: Abolish the boardroom: those who produce the surplus should be the ones who decide what happens to it.

ideologies.name: Workers' self-management
ideologies.blurb: Every enterprise governed by its own workers' council within a socialist and market framework.

ideologies.name: Kibbutz socialism
ideologies.blurb: Communal agricultural settlements holding everything in common, with collective childrearing and no wages.

ideologies.name: Religion of labour
ideologies.blurb: Physical work on the soil is spiritually redemptive; a people renews itself by labouring on its own land.

ideologies.name: Industrial unionism
ideologies.blurb: One union for all workers in an industry, building the new society within the shell of the old.

ideologies.name: Solidarity economy
ideologies.blurb: A patchwork of cooperatives, mutuals and community finance built up alongside the market economy.

ideologies.name: Platform cooperativism
ideologies.blurb: The drivers and couriers should own the app, not be ranked by it.

ideologies.name: Sociocracy
ideologies.blurb: Nested circles making decisions by consent rather than majority, with no one holding a veto over their own domain.

ideologies.name: Distributive workerism
ideologies.blurb: Ownership of the tools spread as widely as possible so that most people work for themselves.

ideologies.name: Distributism
ideologies.blurb: Neither capitalism nor socialism but the widest possible spread of small property — every family with its own workshop or plot.

ideologies.name: Christian democracy
ideologies.blurb: A social market economy guided by subsidiarity and Christian personalism, in ordinary parliamentary politics.

ideologies.name: Christian socialism
ideologies.blurb: The Gospel demands common ownership and the end of competition; socialism is Christianity applied.

ideologies.name: Social Gospel
ideologies.blurb: Sin is social as well as personal; the Kingdom of God is built by reforming slums, factories and laws.

ideologies.name: Liberation theology
ideologies.blurb: God takes a preferential option for the poor, and base communities read scripture as a call to end their oppression.

ideologies.name: Minjung theology
ideologies.blurb: The suffering common people of Korea are themselves the subject of history and of salvation.

ideologies.name: Dalit theology
ideologies.blurb: Christian theology written from outside caste, treating untouchability itself as the central religious question.

ideologies.name: Black liberation theology
ideologies.blurb: God is identified with the oppressed; a theology that ignores Black suffering is not Christian.

ideologies.name: Personalism
ideologies.blurb: The person, never the individual or the collective, is the measure — against both liberal atomism and the mass state.

ideologies.name: Catholic Worker personalism
ideologies.blurb: Houses of hospitality, farming communes and refusal of war, practised directly rather than legislated.

ideologies.name: Solidarism
ideologies.blurb: Society as an organic whole of interdependent estates, obliged to each other by a duty prior to any contract.

ideologies.name: Catholic corporatism
ideologies.blurb: Employers and workers organised together by trade, mediating between the individual and the state.

ideologies.name: Buddhist socialism
ideologies.blurb: Non-attachment applied to property: greed is the root of suffering, so common ownership is a spiritual necessity.

ideologies.name: Buddhist economics
ideologies.blurb: Maximise wellbeing per unit of consumption, not consumption itself; production should stay small and local.

ideologies.name: Islamic socialism
ideologies.blurb: Zakat, the ban on usury and the common ownership of water and pasture read as a socialist programme.

ideologies.name: Sarvodaya
ideologies.blurb: Village self-rule, hand production and truth-force; the means must be as pure as the end.

ideologies.name: Bhoodan
ideologies.blurb: Landlords persuaded to give land away voluntarily, redistribution by moral appeal rather than law.

ideologies.name: Quaker political witness
ideologies.blurb: Decisions by silent discernment and consensus, absolute refusal of war, and plain equality before the light.

ideologies.name: Catholic integralism
ideologies.blurb: The state should be subordinate to the Church in matters of the soul and confessionally Catholic in law.

ideologies.name: Common good constitutionalism
ideologies.blurb: Judges should read law toward substantive moral ends rather than pretend neutrality about the good.

ideologies.name: Christian reconstructionism
ideologies.blurb: The civil law of the Old Testament remains binding; modern states should adopt biblical case law directly.

ideologies.name: Dominionism
ideologies.blurb: Believers are called to take command of every sphere of culture — media, business, government, family.

ideologies.name: Kingdom Now theology
ideologies.blurb: The Church must establish God's kingdom on earth before Christ returns, not wait for him to do it.

ideologies.name: Islamism
ideologies.blurb: Islam is a complete system of life, so the state's law should be derived from the sharia.

ideologies.name: Qutbism
ideologies.blurb: Modern society has reverted to pagan ignorance, so a vanguard must fight it rather than reform it.

ideologies.name: Wilayat al-Faqih
ideologies.blurb: In the absence of the Imam, supreme political authority belongs to the most qualified religious jurist.

ideologies.name: Muslim Brotherhood gradualism
ideologies.blurb: Islamise society from below through preaching, charity and elections before touching the state.

ideologies.name: Caliphate restorationism
ideologies.blurb: Restore a single global caliphate by intellectual and political struggle; nation-states are an imposed fiction.

ideologies.name: Salafi-jihadism
ideologies.blurb: Armed struggle as an individual religious obligation, aimed at restoring a purified early Islamic order.

ideologies.name: Islamic modernism
ideologies.blurb: Reason and revelation are compatible; Islamic law can be reinterpreted for constitutional and scientific modernity.

ideologies.name: Deobandi political thought
ideologies.blurb: Scholarly religious authority and seminary networks guiding society, wary of the state and of Western forms.

ideologies.name: Barelvi political thought
ideologies.blurb: Devotional, saint-venerating Islam defending its practices politically against puritan reformers.

ideologies.name: Hindutva
ideologies.blurb: India defined as a Hindu civilisation, with national belonging measured by cultural and religious descent.

ideologies.name: Integral Humanism
ideologies.blurb: An indigenous Indian third way beyond capitalism and communism, organised around dharma and decentralised production.

ideologies.name: Political Buddhism
ideologies.blurb: The Buddhist religion and the nation defended together, often against a religious minority cast as a threat.

ideologies.name: Sinhalese Buddhist nationalism
ideologies.blurb: Sri Lanka as the island appointed to preserve Buddhism, with the Sinhala people as its guardians.

ideologies.name: Political Confucianism
ideologies.blurb: A tricameral legislature with houses for the people, for cultural continuity, and for Confucian scholars.

ideologies.name: Kokutai
ideologies.blurb: The nation as one family headed by a divine emperor, in an unbroken line since the founding of the world.

ideologies.name: Theodemocracy
ideologies.blurb: God's law revealed through a prophet, ratified by the vote of the people — theocracy and democracy at once.

ideologies.name: Religious Zionism
ideologies.blurb: The return to the land is a stage of redemption, so settlement is a religious commandment.

ideologies.name: Kahanism
ideologies.blurb: A Jewish state governed by halakha with no place for non-Jews in its citizenry.

ideologies.name: Burkean conservatism
ideologies.blurb: Society is an inheritance too complex to redesign; reform slowly, in the grain of what already works.

ideologies.name: Traditionalist conservatism
ideologies.blurb: A permanent moral order exists; culture, custom and religion matter more than markets or constitutions.

ideologies.name: Paleoconservatism
ideologies.blurb: Nation, faith and neighbourhood against globalism, mass immigration and foreign wars.

ideologies.name: Neoconservatism
ideologies.blurb: American power used actively to spread democratic capitalism, with a moralised view of foreign policy.

ideologies.name: Straussianism
ideologies.blurb: Classical political philosophy read esoterically, against relativism and in defence of the regime's noble myths.

ideologies.name: One Nation conservatism
ideologies.blurb: The privileged owe obligations to the poor; the nation must not be allowed to split into two.

ideologies.name: High Toryism
ideologies.blurb: Church, Crown and land as the settled order, sceptical of commerce and of democracy alike.

ideologies.name: Red Toryism
ideologies.blurb: Against both the market state and the welfare state — rebuild associations, guilds and local ownership.

ideologies.name: Compassionate conservatism
ideologies.blurb: Deliver welfare through churches and charities rather than the state, without abandoning the poor.

ideologies.name: Gaullism
ideologies.blurb: A strong executive and an independent nation, above party and outside every bloc.

ideologies.name: National conservatism
ideologies.blurb: A world of independent nations, each with its own religious tradition, against transnational governance.

ideologies.name: Postliberalism
ideologies.blurb: Liberalism failed because it succeeded — its individualism dissolved the communities people actually need.

ideologies.name: Legitimism
ideologies.blurb: The rightful dynasty was deposed unlawfully and its restoration is the only legitimate order.

ideologies.name: Carlism
ideologies.blurb: God, fatherland, local charters and king — a traditionalist monarchism defending regional liberties.

ideologies.name: Jacobitism
ideologies.blurb: The Stuart line remains the true sovereign; every subsequent settlement is usurpation.

ideologies.name: Absolute monarchism
ideologies.blurb: Sovereignty undivided in one person, answerable to God alone and to no assembly.

ideologies.name: Constitutional monarchism
ideologies.blurb: A hereditary head of state as continuity and symbol, with real power in an elected parliament.

ideologies.name: Neofeudalism

ideologies.name: Bioregionalism

ideologies.blurb: Spirit wrestlers refusing the state, the army and private property, living communally on the land.

ideologies.name: Anabaptist withdrawal
ideologies.blurb: A separate community of the faithful, refusing oaths, arms and worldly office entirely.

ideologies.name: Neo-tribalism
ideologies.blurb: Humans evolved for small bands; political life should be rebuilt at that scale.

ideologies.name: Human-scale politics
ideologies.blurb: Institutions stop working past the number of people you can actually know; keep everything below it.

ideologies.name: Village republic
ideologies.blurb: Each village a self-sufficient republic, with the wider state existing only to serve it.

ideologies.name: Third Way
ideologies.blurb: Beyond left and right — market mechanisms delivering social goals, with rights matched by responsibilities.

ideologies.name: New Democrat centrism
ideologies.blurb: Fiscal discipline, welfare conditionality and free trade paired with social liberalism.

ideologies.name: Radical centrism
ideologies.blurb: Take the best ideas from both sides and implement them aggressively, unbound by tribal loyalty.

ideologies.name: Liberal corporatism
ideologies.blurb: Government, employers and unions bargaining national policy together at one table.

ideologies.name: Rhenish capitalism
ideologies.blurb: Patient bank finance, works councils and long-term ownership rather than shareholder pressure.

ideologies.name: Neue Mitte
ideologies.blurb: Social democracy modernised for a service economy — activate, retrain and reduce transfers.

ideologies.name: Purple politics
ideologies.blurb: Liberal on the economy and liberal on culture, governing by coalition across the old divide.

ideologies.name: Syncretic politics
ideologies.blurb: Deliberately combine positions from opposed traditions, treating the left-right axis as obsolete.

ideologies.name: Technocratic centrism
ideologies.blurb: Politics as competent administration; most questions have a correct answer that experts can find.

ideologies.name: Big-tent pragmatism
ideologies.blurb: Whatever works — no fixed doctrine, judged case by case on outcomes.

ideologies.name: Christian democratic centrism
ideologies.blurb: The social market anchored in personalism and subsidiarity, governing from the middle.

ideologies.name: Post-left anarchy
ideologies.blurb: Drop the leftist baggage — morality, organisation, work and the workers' movement — and keep the anarchy.

ideologies.name: Individualist nihilism
ideologies.blurb: No values survive scrutiny, so act from your own will and expect nothing to follow.

ideologies.name: Refusal of work
ideologies.blurb: The work ethic is the ruling class's best invention; the demand should be less work, not more jobs.

ideologies.name: Zerowork
ideologies.blurb: Sabotage, absenteeism and go-slows read as the real content of class struggle.

ideologies.name: Anti-work politics
ideologies.blurb: Most jobs are pointless and coercive; the goal is to need far fewer of them.

ideologies.name: Conscious apoliticism
ideologies.blurb: Politics corrupts whatever it touches; the honest response is to refuse participation entirely.

ideologies.name: Discordianism
ideologies.blurb: Treat all order as a joke and all belief as provisional; disrupt certainty wherever you find it.

ideologies.name: Multiple-name politics
ideologies.blurb: Everyone adopts the same pseudonym so that authorship, celebrity and identity stop functioning.

ideologies.name: Absurdist politics
ideologies.blurb: Run the joke campaign; the absurdity is the critique.

ideologies.name: Accelerationist nihilism
ideologies.blurb: There is nothing to save and nothing to build; watch it burn faster.

ideologies.name: Political quietism
ideologies.blurb: Cultivate your own garden; public life is beyond repair and beneath attention.

ideologies.name: Union of egoists
ideologies.blurb: Association only for as long as it serves each party, dissolved the moment it does not.

ideologies.name: Informal organisation
ideologies.blurb: Permanent structures breed bureaucrats; act in temporary informal groupings and dissolve them.

ideologies.name: Détournement politics
ideologies.blurb: Hijack the culture's own images and turn them against it.

ideologies.name: Owenism
ideologies.blurb: Character is formed by environment, so build model communities of cooperation and the new person follows.

ideologies.name: Fourierism
ideologies.blurb: Organise work around the passions so labour becomes attractive; twelve hundred people to a phalanstery.

ideologies.name: Saint-Simonianism
ideologies.blurb: Rule by industrialists, engineers and bankers organising production for all, replacing government of men with administration of things.

ideologies.name: Icarianism
ideologies.blurb: A peaceful communist colony run by elected committees, with everything owned and decided in common.

ideologies.name: Blanquism
ideologies.blurb: A small conspiratorial band seizes power in a coup and holds a temporary dictatorship until society is remade.

ideologies.name: Chartism
ideologies.blurb: Universal male suffrage, secret ballots and paid MPs — political democracy as the workers' first demand.

ideologies.name: Proudhonian federalism
ideologies.blurb: Society built upward by contract between communes and workshops, never downward from a capital.

ideologies.name: Shaker communalism
ideologies.blurb: Celibate communal villages holding all property in common, with women and men governing equally.

ideologies.name: Oneida perfectionism
ideologies.blurb: A community practising complex marriage and communal childrearing, holding that perfection is attainable now.

ideologies.name: Land and Freedom
ideologies.blurb: All land to the peasant communes and full political liberty, pursued by agitation and then by terror.

ideologies.name: Morrisite socialism
ideologies.blurb: A society of craft, beauty and pleasurable work, with machines used only to spare drudgery.

ideologies.name: Ruskinian social criticism
ideologies.blurb: There is no wealth but life; judge an economy by the quality of the lives and things it produces.

ideologies.name: Utopian colony socialism
ideologies.blurb: Found the ideal settlement somewhere cheap and let its example convert the world.

ideologies.name: Peaceful communism
ideologies.blurb: Communism arriving by persuasion and example, with violence rejected as self-defeating.

ideologies.name: Associationist land reform
ideologies.blurb: Cooperative associations settled on land held in common trust, combining two nineteenth-century reforms.

ideologies.name: Sortition
ideologies.blurb: Fill offices by random selection from the citizenry; elections produce an aristocracy, lotteries a sample.

ideologies.name: Citizens' assembly maximalism
ideologies.blurb: Randomly selected deliberating assemblies should decide the questions parliaments cannot.

ideologies.name: Liquid democracy
ideologies.blurb: Vote yourself or delegate your vote to whoever you trust on that issue, and revoke it at any time.

ideologies.name: Delegative democracy
ideologies.blurb: Mandated, instantly recallable delegates rather than representatives with independent judgement.

ideologies.name: Futarchy
ideologies.blurb: Vote on values, bet on beliefs — elect the goal, then let prediction markets pick the policy.

ideologies.name: Epistocracy
ideologies.blurb: Weight political power by demonstrated competence; universal suffrage produces uninformed harm.

ideologies.name: Consociationalism
ideologies.blurb: Divided societies governed by grand coalition, mutual veto and segmental autonomy.

ideologies.name: Directorial government
ideologies.blurb: A collegial executive of equals with a rotating chair, and no single head of government at all.

ideologies.name: Anational federalism
ideologies.blurb: Federate by function and voluntary association rather than by territory or nationality.

ideologies.name: Constitutional patriotism
ideologies.blurb: Loyalty owed to a set of democratic principles rather than to a people, a history or a soil.

ideologies.name: Direct democracy maximalism
ideologies.blurb: Referendums on everything; representatives are an unnecessary filter between people and decisions.

ideologies.name: Mixed constitution
ideologies.blurb: Balance monarchy, aristocracy and democracy against each other so that none can dominate.

ideologies.name: LaRouchism
ideologies.blurb: Physical-economic development by great infrastructure projects, wrapped in a conspiratorial history of civilisation.

ideologies.name: Theosophical politics
ideologies.blurb: Spiritual evolution guiding social reform — universal brotherhood, home rule and esoteric hierarchy together.

ideologies.name: Threefold Social Order
ideologies.blurb: Split society into three independent spheres — liberty in culture, equality in law, fraternity in the economy.

ideologies.name: Rastafari politics
ideologies.blurb: Repatriation to Africa, rejection of Babylon's institutions, and a divine African monarch.

ideologies.name: Cargo cult movements
ideologies.blurb: Ritual and prophecy organised to bring back the goods and dignity that colonisation took away.

ideologies.name: Taiping ideology
ideologies.blurb: A Christian-inflected heavenly kingdom with land held in common and the sexes strictly separated.

ideologies.name: Sovereign citizen ideology
ideologies.blurb: Claim that government authority rests on a contract you can unilaterally revoke through the right paperwork.

ideologies.name: Freeman on the land
ideologies.blurb: A legal-fiction theory holding that statutes bind only those who consent to be bound by them.

ideologies.name: Patriot constitutionalism
ideologies.blurb: The original constitution as sacred text, defended by an armed citizenry against a lawless federal government.

ideologies.name: Survivalist politics
ideologies.blurb: Collapse is coming; the political unit that matters is the household that can feed and defend itself.

ideologies.name: Neo-pagan politics
ideologies.blurb: Pre-Christian religion revived as a political identity of land, ancestry and seasonal cycle.

ideologies.name: Wiccan political theology
ideologies.blurb: Harm none, and a politics of consent, ecology and the divine feminine following from it.

ideologies.name: Millenarian revolutionism
ideologies.blurb: The old world is about to end in judgement, and the elect must act now to bring the new one in.

ideologies.name: Ranterism
ideologies.blurb: God is in everything and so nothing is sin; property, clergy and law are all abolished at once.

ideologies.name: Contactee politics
ideologies.blurb: Advanced extraterrestrials as the model and the coming solution to earthly government.

ideologies.name: Land and money reform
ideologies.blurb: Tax land rent and let money decay — the two monopolies attacked together.

ideologies.name: Distributive monarchism
ideologies.blurb: A king above, small property below, and nothing much in between.

ideologies.name: Esoteric nationalism
ideologies.blurb: The nation as a spiritual entity with a hidden destiny, accessible through myth and initiation.

ideologies.name: Monastic politics
ideologies.blurb: Withdraw into a disciplined religious community and let it outlast the collapsing world outside.

ideologies.name: Pirate politics
ideologies.blurb: Copyright reform, privacy and transparency as the organising axis of politics.

ideologies.name: Cyberdelic politics
ideologies.blurb: Psychedelics and computer networks as twin technologies of consciousness and liberation.
